Review #3: The Balvenie DoubleWood 12 year old

The Balvenie DoubleWood 12 year old

Single Malt Scotch Whisky

thedersy1’s third review

43% ABV

Served into a glencairn, neat and water added later.

Color: Gold

Nose: Rich fruits, vanilla, hint of pepper, little bit of spiciness and heat on the nose. With water some delicate floral notes arise from amongst the fruit and spice.

Palate: Sherry up front. Syrupy fruits, vanilla and butterscotch. Lightly oily mouthfeel that seems to be common among sherried whiskies I've had. I don't think the palate on this holds up that well to the addition of water. It seems to kind of blur the lines between a lot of these various sweet flavor notes.

Finish: Short-Medium, drying finish. There's a level of peppery spice that appears in the finish that decreases the longer it rests. With the addition of water the spice almost completely disappears and the finish seems to extend a little bit.

Development: After resting for a little bit the bourbon influences begin to take a back seat to the sherry. While the butterscotch and vanilla flavors remain they seem to meld together with the dark fruits and sherry sweetness. This is definitely more of a dessert whisky, I'd say.

82/100

I definitely agree, this is an awesome scotch for beginners. It is very middle of the road in terms of flavor, leaning a bit more heavily on the sherry side of things. It's unoffensive, although I have to say when I first tried this (what seems like ages ago now, even though it was maybe 4 months ago) the peppery kick hit me pretty hard and put me off for a bit. I tried this first as a part of a 5 part flight at a bar, and as time went on and the spirit mellowed out I found myself liking it better than the rest of the ones I tried that night (Macallan 12, Glenlivet 12, Glenfiddich 12, and Cardhu 12). This is definitely a spirit that benefits from resting a few minutes.

Originally bought this at $46 for a bottle. Would I buy this again? No, not even at $40. Why? Not because it isn't good, but because it isn't nearly as exciting or challenging as I'd like. It's mellow and enjoyable, but so are a lot of cheap blends and bourbons, and at the price I'd much rather reach for a bottle of Glenfarclas 12 (review to come eventually). I respect the DoubleWood for holding the door open for myself and many others that were just beginning their malt journeys, but alas it must stay at the door and hold it open, and I don't plan on hanging out by the door all night.

What’s to come: Going to try and review things in the order I received them, what comes next is: Macallan 12, Jura Collection (Jura 10yr Origin, Superstition, Diurach's Own 16yr), Glenlivet Nadurra 16 year old, Bunnahabhain 12, and Glenfarclas 12 (this one will be quite a ways away). Until next time, cheers!

If I can immediately tell that you have custom CSS, you've used to much CSS. I disable it because it's absolutely rediculous to ask me to learn a new interface for every subverse I subscribe to. There are also many that are incredibly taxing on the eyes, and as someone who spends most for his day on a computer, I need themes to be easy on the eyes.

Acceptable use includes things like custom sidebar buttons to make searching by tag easier, replacing post tags with icons, custom header images, custom vote arrows, custom mouse over text for vote arrows, things like creating the option to make spoiler text, and custom text for things like the "are you sure you want to report this post" message.

Unacceptable uses include any changes to layout(On Reddit, moving the login button was a big one), any changes to functionality(hiding downvote arrows, or going full SRS and switching up and down vote arrows), causing eyestrain, appending text on to posts, or breaking common add-on functionality(many subreddits removed Reddit Enhancement Suite's open all images button).

On Reddit(with Reddit Enhancement Suite), I would leave CSS enabled, and then disable per-subreddit as I encountered bad CSS, so that I wouldn't miss any ones with extra functionality(/r/steamgameswap), and any that weren't offensive enough would still function. Unfortunately, that is not a luxury afforded to me on Voat currently, so all CSS is disabled. When we get the per-subverse option, or a RES equivalent, I'll reenable the CSS you've worked so hard on, for any subverses worth using it on.

tl;dr: Change is bad, unless it specifically improves on the old design.
